notes.title: Rangers, it’s time to head back into Faremont National Park: Early Access Content Update 2 is now live!

items.text: This update brings you closer to the wildlife of Faremont with new animal species, new ways to interact with animals, new ranger tools, and a variety of additional callouts. Your day-to-day work in the park just got even wilder.

With Content Update 2, wildlife now plays a bigger role in your ranger duties. The new Animal Interaction System allows you to do more than observe animals from a distance. You can now help injured wildlife, free animals caught in traps, and take part in important tracking tasks across the park.

To support these new duties, Update 2 introduces two new tools: the tranquilizer gun and the VHF receiver. The tranquilizer gun allows you to sedate injured or trapped animals from a safe distance, so you can examine, treat, or free them without putting yourself in danger. The VHF receiver helps you track animals fitted with GPS transmitters, making wildlife monitoring an even more hands-on part of your work as a ranger.

notes.title: 🦬 New animals in Faremont National Park

items.text: Three new animal species have made their way into Faremont with Update 2.

The mighty bison has joined the park as a true American icon, offering an impressive new sight for visitors and rangers alike. Feral hogs can now be found roaming the forests, adding even more life to Faremont’s wilder areas. And if you are lucky, you might spot the elusive bobcat somewhere across the hills and mountain slopes of the park.
Keep your eyes open, rangers. Some encounters may be easier to find than others.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/4d1148b38ee054997aabc961431d8d93b101fb6d.png"]
Content Update 2 introduces a variety of new callouts and dynamic events, adding more variety to your daily ranger routine.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/8a43914c8d46456f5e6cf9bef9d1e0e17238e7a7.jpg"]
Reports of traps found in certain areas have reached ranger HQ. Your task is to locate and dismantle them before they become a danger to visitors or wildlife.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/5bd5c28758c67041cffec4d81f91322be3102b97.jpg"]
Sometimes, the worst has already happened. An animal has been caught in a trap and needs your help immediately. Track it down, tranquilize it with your tranquilizer gun, and set it free.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/f18286bec465bb19ef34de19f8c3e74ad3f7d1b6.jpg"]
Hikers have reported injured wild animals in the park. Find the animal, sedate it safely, and examine and treat its injuries.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/786c95d8d01f2788749271388007dedfdbdaf70e.jpg"]
Some animals in Faremont are part of wildlife studies and have been fitted with GPS transmitters. Use your VHF receiver to locate the animal, sedate it, and remove the device to gather data.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/b57cc7d745567194a331ef1bb3325dd9b44ee14c.jpg"]
Animal care is not the only new responsibility in Update 2. Faremont’s plant life also needs your attention.
Invasive plant species threaten the park’s ecosystem. With the new root puller, you can remove them whenever and wherever you find them.

Some areas of the park are ready to be restored with new vegetation. Collect seedlings of flora native to Faremont and plant them in designated spots across the map. Don’t forget to check back every now and then to watch your new plants grow!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/33ed2802c759ed61c1177e9ffd2fd49929e6262c.jpg"]
Of course, keeping Faremont clean, safe, and peaceful also means dealing with visitors who do not always follow the rules.

Some camper groups leave campsites in a rough state. Document the damage with your camera, deal with those responsible at your own discretion, and close the campsite until you have repaired the damage, cleaned up the trash, and restored the area.
Some visitors bring a little too much noise into the wild. If loud music becomes a nuisance to other visitors or wildlife, it is your duty to find the source and restore some peace and quiet.

Even with designated waste disposal points available throughout the park, some visitors still leave trash behind. Remind them that littering not only violates park rules, but can also become a danger to wildlife and to themselves.
Alongside the new animals, tools, callouts, and wildlife interactions, Update 2 also includes a range of additional fixes and quality-of-life improvements based on your feedback.

One highly requested addition is the new hop ability. While Ranger’s Path is not suddenly turning into a full platforming adventure, you can now perform a small hop to make movement through Faremont feel a little smoother and more responsive.

We’ve also worked on various smaller improvements, fixes, and adjustments across the game to make your ranger duties feel better while exploring the park, completing callouts, and keeping Faremont safe for visitors and wildlife.
Thank you to everyone who keeps sharing suggestions, bug reports, and feedback with us. Your input continues to help us improve Ranger’s Path throughout Early Access.

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/8cbc9c80eecff5a290d0694e4eb8e09a4dc07241.jpg"]

While work on Update 2 continues, we wanted to release a smaller in-between patch for Ranger’s Path: National Park Simulator, focused on quality-of-life improvements, bug fixes, and a few behind-the-scenes adjustments.

Update 1.11 is not a major content update, but it brings several improvements that should make your time in Faremont National Park smoother and more comfortable while we continue working on the next bigger update.

As always, thank you for your feedback, bug reports, suggestions, and discussions here on Steam. Your input helps us understand what matters most to the community and continues to guide our work during Early Access.
One of the main additions in Update 1.11 is the new pause feature.

We know many of you asked for more control during your shift, especially when you need to step away for a moment, check something, or simply take a short break without time continuing to move in the background.
With Update 1.11, you can now pause the game, making ranger life in Faremont a little more relaxed.
We’ve also updated the info panel picture, giving this part of the UI a refreshed look and improving the overall presentation.
Update 1.11 also includes several smaller fixes and improvements, including:
Added Steam Cloud Save
Performance improvements, especially on lower-end systems
Mission-related bug fixes
Input system bug fixes
Added more openings in fences to improve map navigation
Adjusted running speed and gravity scale balancing
Smaller quality-of-life changes
Minor polish and stability improvements

We know many of you are looking forward to Update 2, and we’re excited to share more about it when the time is right. You can get a sneak peek for our upcoming update on our Early Access Roadmap. Until then, Update 1.11 should help improve the current Early Access experience and address several of the issues reported by the community.
Please keep sharing your feedback with us here on Steam. It helps us a lot during development and plays an important role in shaping the game.

And if you’re enjoying your time in Faremont National Park, leaving a Steam review is one of the best ways to support the game during Early Access. It helps new players discover Ranger’s Path and helps us continue building the game together with the community. 🫶
Thank you again for being part of the journey. 💚
See you out on the trails, rangers. 🏕️

notes.title: Rangers, report back for duty – Early Access Content Update 1 is now live!

items.text: Faremont National Park is busier than ever, with new duties and responsibilities.
With this update, your role as a ranger expands, introducing new tasks across the park, alongside the Park Review Score system and a new off-road vehicle to support your patrols.

With Update 1, your work as a ranger truly shapes Faremont National Park. The Park Review Score reflects the overall health and quality of the park, tying together everything you do out in the field. By maintaining trails, responding to callouts, and taking care of the environment, you steadily improve the park’s reputation and unlock new rewards along the way. What you protect today will define the park of tomorrow.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/f332625a02bed8873bd0fbf4101a615349140047.png"]

While we love welcoming new visitors to the park, not everyone follows the rules. The Backpack Search callout introduces new situations that require careful observation and attention to detail. As a ranger, you will inspect visitors and uncover illegal activities taking place within the park.

This includes tracking illegal drone operators by spotting drones in the sky and identifying their controllers, catching vandals in the act of spraying benches, and locating poachers who disturb protected flora. Keeping Faremont safe now depends more than ever on your awareness and instincts.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/1c444d852f573d8396ac6970f7e8821258fe4d9f.jpg"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/98741dd757d7a7202f55dcac511e6b6721287f41.jpg"]

With the Flora Survey callout, you take on the role of monitoring the health of plant life across the park. You will be dispatched to specific areas where you must locate designated flora using your Ranger Sense, assess their condition, and take action if necessary. Every inspection contributes to preserving the balance of the ecosystem and ensuring that Faremont National Park remains a thriving natural habitat.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/b0091fd380b9eb8fa108173b1b208c89f3e48442.jpg"]

The Restock callout focuses on keeping the park functional and welcoming for visitors. You will collect supplies from ranger facilities and distribute them to locations such as trailheads, information panels, and campsites. By ensuring that maps, brochures, and campfire supplies are always available, you help create a smooth and enjoyable experience for everyone exploring Faremont National Park.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/8b29ded35fb2ada57e7b90200ba247925b37d17e.jpg"]

The Transport callout introduces logistics-focused tasks that are essential for daily park operations. You will gather items from multiple locations and deliver them to a central destination, supporting activities such as weather data collection, waste management, and campsite maintenance. While these tasks may seem menial, they are the kind of behind-the-scenes work that keeps the park running smoothly and ensures everything is where it needs to be.

notes.title: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/65fd9b1b37edb4e0a9780a51bbaf89987f0204c4.jpg"]🛻 New Vehicle: Trailhawk Summit Utility Vehicle

items.text: To support your expanded duties, Update 1 introduces the Trailhawk Summit Utility Vehicle, a rugged and reliable vehicle designed for off-road patrols. Compared to the pickup truck, it offers improved maneuverability and handling on rough terrain, making it especially useful on forest trails and uneven ground. Whether you are responding to a callout or exploring remote areas of the park, the Jeep ensures you can get there with confidence.

III. Bug Fixes
Critical Fixes

Early Access Update 1 marks a major step in shaping Faremont National Park into a living, breathing park. From law enforcement to conservation and logistics, your responsibilities as a ranger have grown, and so has your impact on the park.
Your continued feedback will help us guide the future of Ranger’s Path, and we’re excited to keep building this journey together.

we’re back with another update!

First of all, a huge thank you to everyone who continues exploring the park, sharing feedback, reporting issues and leaving reviews. Your support really helps us shape Ranger’s Path: National Park Simulator during Early Access 💚
Today we’re releasing Patch V1.0.4, which focuses on gameplay flow improvements, stability, performance optimizations and a number of bug fixes reported by the community.
We’ve also started to implement some balancing changes that should make daily routines in the park feel more natural and less repetitive.
Added FSR support to provide more performance options across a wider range of hardware
Adjusted Time of Day speed and overall day length. Daytime is now longer after completing the onboarding missions
Improved litter spawning balance across the map to reduce overly frequent respawns in maintained areas
Improved NPC navigation behavior and reduced cases where characters avoided invisible spots
General performance improvements and memory optimizations
Additional gameplay flow adjustments and overall polish
Fixed an issue where the Litter Picker auto targeting could cause incorrect pickup behavior
Fixed excessive litter spawning after completing all main missions
Fixed an issue where some interactable objects could become stuck, including vehicles in rare cases
Fixed excessive collision on fallen trees blocking trails
Fixed animal behavior not being detected correctly by the camera in certain situations
Fixed various mission spawned objects not saving their state correctly, such as footsteps
Fixed an issue where the Violet Trail could not be properly opened after repair
Fixed edge cases where NPCs could appear floating above the ground
Fixed material artifacts visible on the bear in some LOD levels
Improved navigation consistency for NPC movement across the park
Fixed localization overflow in Spanish and Latin American Spanish tablet UI
Fixed a keybind collision between Hat toggle and Unstuck on gamepad. Tapping now switches the hat while holding the button unstucks the player
We are already working on further patches and improvements based on your feedback.
This includes continued balancing of gameplay pacing, additional quality of life improvements, performance work and of course new content updates during Early Access.
If you haven’t already, make sure to check out our roadmap to get a first glimpse of what’s coming next.
Once again, thank you all! We can't wait to see how Faremont National Park evolves throughout Early Access, with you as part of our Faremont National Park Service!

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45730064/93d08200fb0d97873b81eb8023c2c7f8aaa83576.jpg"]
Faremont National Park Service, reporting for duty!

Thank you to everyone who jumped into Ranger’s Path: National Park Simulator yesterday with the start of our Early Access journey. Your feedback, bug reports, and suggestions have been incredibly helpful already. 🌲
Today we’re releasing our first hotfix, addressing several issues reported by you shortly after launch.
Gameplay & Progression
Fixed an issue where the respawn button did not function correctly
Fixed a hard lock that could occur in the "Trail of Breadcrumbs" quest when picking up an item at 21:00
Fixed a VIP quest objective becoming stuck if obstacles were cleared earlier than intended
Fixed an issue where a lost visitor would not leave the area after being reprimanded
UI & Controls
Fixed a partial soft lock that could occur when switching tools in the tool wheel before using another tool
Localization & Audio
Fixed an issue where Effy’s dialogue remained in English despite German audio being selected
Fixed incorrect rendering of Chinese characters
Fixed a typo in the "Lost Visitor" quest
Visual Fixes
Fixed an issue with the flag placement on a truck

Early Access is a collaborative journey, and your reports are helping us improve the experience quickly. Please continue sharing feedback, bugs, and suggestions with us through the Steam forums or our Discord community.
More updates, fixes, and new content are already in the works. 🌿
See you out on the trails, rangers. 🏕️
